capex.heading: Capital Expenditures
capex.text:
From time to time, we make capital expenditures to maintain or improve our aircraft. These expenditures include the cost of major overhauls necessary to place an aircraft in service and modifications made at the request of lessees. For the three months ended May 31, 2025 and 2024, we incurred a total of $13.7 million and $9.0 million, respectively, of capital expenditures, including lease incentives, related to the improvement of aircraft.

As of May 31, 2025, the weighted average age by Net Book Value of our aircraft was approximately 8.9 years. In general, the costs of operating an aircraft, including maintenance expenditures, increase with the age of the aircraft. Our lease agreements call for the lessee to be primarily responsible for maintaining the aircraft. Our leases may require the lessee to make periodic payments to us during the lease term to provide reserves for future major maintenance events. Provided a lessee performs scheduled maintenance of the aircraft, we are required to reimburse the lessee for scheduled maintenance payments. In certain cases, we are also required to make lessor contributions, in excess of amounts a lessee may have paid, towards the costs of maintenance events performed by or on behalf of the lessee.

capex.text:
From time to time, we make capital expenditures to maintain or improve our aircraft. These expenditures include the cost of major overhauls necessary to place an aircraft in service and modifications made at the request of lessees. For the six months ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, we incurred a total of $4.8 million and $14.2 million, respectively, of capital expenditures, including lease incentives, related to the improvement of aircraft.

As of August 31, 2026, the weighted average age of our aircraft, by Net Book Value, of our aircraft was approximately 9.0 years. In general, the costs of operating an aircraft, including maintenance expenditures, increases as aircraft age. Our lease agreements generally require the lessee to be primarily responsible for maintaining the aircraft.

Maintenance reserves are generally paid by the lessee to provide for future major maintenance events. Provided a lessee performs scheduled maintenance of the aircraft, we are required to reimburse the lessee for qualifying maintenance payments. In certain cases, we are also required to make lessor contributions, in excess of amounts a lessee may have paid, towards the costs of maintenance events performed by or on behalf of the lessee.

net sales.heading: Revenues:
net sales.text:
Total revenues increased $55.4 million, attributable to:

Lease rental revenue decreased $3.3 million, primarily attributable to:

• a $16.4 million decrease related to the sale of 32 aircraft and other flight equipment since September 1, 2025;

• a $9.7 million decrease related to early lease terminations, including terminations associated with 2 customers that either filed for bankruptcy protection or ceased operations; and

• a $5.0 million decrease due to lease extensions, amendments, transitions and other changes.

This was partially offset by an increase of $27.9 million related to 42 aircraft purchased since September 1, 2025.

Amortization of lease premiums, discounts and lease incentives :

The amortization of lease incentives decreased $7.1 million, primarily due to early lease terminations and the associated reversal of lease incentive liabilities during the three months ended August 31, 2026.

Maintenance revenue. For the three months ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, we recorded $43.0 million and $9.7 million of maintenance revenue, respectively, primarily from maintenance payments received by us and recognized into income in connection with scheduled aircraft lease expirations, early lease terminations and aircraft returns.

intro.text: Unless the context suggests otherwise, references in this Annual Report to “Aircastle,” the “Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our” refer to Aircastle Limited and its subsidiaries. Throughout this Annual Report, when we refer to our aircraft, we include aircraft that we have transferred into grantor trusts or similar entities for purposes of financing such assets through term financings. These grantor trusts or similar entities are consolidated for purposes of our financial statements. All amounts in this Annual Report are expressed in U.S. dollars and the financial statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“U.S. GAAP”).

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
